messages.text: Hi Prof. Petrov, hope the weekend is treating you well. I’m John Doe from Chen’s group; we’re building Link for the HackMIT/Dropbox event in September.
We’ve got a pretty clean pipeline for resolving free-text interests to a concept ontology, and I was wondering if you’d be open to advising on a workshop paper about the method?

Hello John. Interesting scope. Do you have a rough one-page summary of the approach and any preliminary results you can share by Tuesday? I am generally available on Thursdays for quick calls or reviews.
Absolutely. I’ll have that over to you before end of day Tue. Quick heads-up: we’re keeping it very local (no cloud APIs) for privacy reasons, so the evals are all on our own infra.
That is a strong constraint to build around. Please include the trade-offs you observed with local inference in that summary as well; context matters for the method description.
Will do. I’m drafting it now so I can get your eyes on the framing before I finalize the numbers. Thanks for being so quick to respond, by the way.
You are welcome. Keep it focused on the resolution logic itself rather than the application wrapper; that is where the contribution lies for a workshop audience. Best, Sofia
Understood. I’ll strip the app UI details out and focus on the ontology mapping and scoring. I’ll send that one-pager over in about two days.
